C02_S03: UNIVERSAL REGULARIZED DICKE MIXTURE COMPILER
7 October UTC / 8 October Brisbane, 2026. Separate post-freeze addendum.
Root proposed uniform symmetric regularization; this worker reconstructed the
moment, positivity, error and bit arguments. C08_S03 proposed the rational pure
Bloch chart and dyadic sampling upgrade and independently checked its identity.
No previous proof, INITIAL, peer artifact, or implementation is edited.

THE PRECISE INTERFACE AND CLAIM
Let n>=1 and rho=sum_(k=0)^n pi_k |D_n,k><D_n,k|, pi>=0, sum pi=1.
PROMISE: there is a probability measure mu on [0,1] such that
 pi_k=integral binom(n,k)x^k(1-x)^(n-k) mu(dx).
This is equivalent to full separability for a state supported in the symmetric
space and diagonal in the Dicke basis. It is an input promise, not a membership
test. Positivity and symmetric support force every product vector in a pure
separable decomposition to have identical one-site factors; a common phase
twirl then gives precisely this binomial-measure representation. Conversely
the representation and phase averaging give a separable decomposition.

The input law is supplied either (a) as an EXACT RATIONAL normalized probability
vector of total bit length L, or (b) by an EXPLICIT charged acquisition procedure
which, on integer P, returns rational estimates of every pi_k with certified
absolute error <=2^-P and with stated bit/time cost A(n,L,P). No cost-free real
law, relative accuracy on tiny probabilities, or efficient acquisition of every
abstract computable law is asserted. In case (b), the compiler cost is A at
polynomial precision plus polynomial bit work. A polynomial total cost follows
only when the specified acquisition procedure has a polynomial cost bound.

For rational 0<epsilon<=1, put d=floor(n/2)+1 and M=d(n+1).
The compiler returns at most M pure iid n-qubit product labels and nonnegative
classical weights (zero-weight labels can be removed), with trace distance
<=epsilon from rho. Two output formats:

 I. Exact rational nodes/weights, exact algebraic one-qubit coherent descriptors
    using square roots and a primitive (n+1)st root of unity. Error <=epsilon/4.
 II. Exact rational 2x2 rank-one positive one-qubit density matrices, and common
     dyadic nonnegative weights summing to1. Error <=epsilon/2. Each classical
     label is sampled EXACTLY with a fixed polynomial number of fair bits.

magnitude but finite rational encoding. Abstract unencoded real inputs are

VERDICT AND EXACT SCOPE

PASS for C02_S03's frozen UNIVERSAL_REGULARIZED_COMPILER.txt, positive optimal
domain extension, and separate signed-domain composition. This is a constructive
all-n finite-bit theorem conditional on the precise separability/input promise,
not a membership algorithm. The underlying exact positive-domain theorem is an
imported, internally accepted premise. Its large finite-prefix campaign was not
reexecuted here. Negative-domain existence is independently reconstructed below.

The compiler returns at most (floor(n/2)+1)(n+1) positive pure iid labels.
Format I has exact rational nodes/weights, algebraic pure local descriptors,
and trace distance <=epsilon/4. Format II has exact rational rank-one local
density matrices, common dyadic weights, and trace distance <=epsilon/2.
Its label sampler uses an exact bounded number of fair bits. Post-acquisition
bit work is polynomial in n, encoded input length, and log(1/epsilon).
Physical preparation, generic acquisition of an unencoded real state, a dense
2^n output, practical polynomial degree, external validation and priority are
not certified by this audit.
